description: Phase 3 review round 1 for the MDN epic (JMAP-7lr). 7 reviewers fire simultaneously covering correctness, maintainability, efficiency, elegance, readability, decisions, and calibration.
notes:
SEC4 readability review complete. Four P4 issues filed: JMAP-5ugd (TODO comment in MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS), JMAP-iraq (wrong spec section §2.1 vs §3.1 in handle_mdn_send Step 3 comment), JMAP-26ai (test oracle does not cite definition site for finalRecipient value), JMAP-w8zx (rfc822 address-type prefix unexplained in common/mod.rs). Module-level doc, algorithm step comments, oracle comments for parse tests, and Disposition heuristic explanation are all adequate.
SEC0 correctness review complete. 2 P0 bugs filed: JMAP-91zr (handle_mdn_send never validates that the request 'using' array contains both urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn and urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail as required by draft §2.1), JMAP-6ljq (null forEmailId in MDN/send falls through to backend which returns notFound, but spec requires invalidProperties for a MUST NOT be null violation). All other checks passed: onSuccessUpdateEmail coverage is correct (every send key verified), $mdnsent pre-check is correct keyword and casing, Email/set companion structure is correct (same call_id, correct accountId/oldState/newState, nulls for empty maps), MDN/parse returns null not empty for absent collections, enum wire values match spec exactly, parse result flows correctly, no panics in library code (dnt_address.unwrap() in test backend is guarded), using validation gap is only at handler level not dispatcher level, TOCTOU in $mdnsent pre-check is acknowledged inherent limitation not a P0, mdn_send_success test does verify $mdnsent is stamped (lines 149-163).
Confidence: 30% chance of missed real bug. Reasoning: The implementation is moderate complexity (~480 lines handler + ~250 lines types). Reviewers found real engineering issues (two email round-trips per send entry, full blob load before parse heuristic, TODO comment violating CLAUDE.md). One genuine spec conformance gap the other agents appear to have missed: spec §2 says forEmailId MUST NOT be null for MDN/send. The handler at mdn.rs:247 uses 'if let Some(ref for_email_id) = mdn.for_email_id' -- when None, the entry bypasses the dollar-mdnsent pre-check and lands in remaining_send, delegating the null check to the backend. The MemoryBackend handles it as notFound, but the spec requires this to be an invalidProperties error from the handler, not a backend-delegation. This is a spec conformance bug at P2 level. Are we running out of real complaints? Mostly yes. JMAP-bkqp (fully-qualified types in struct fields) is a pure bikeshed with no engineering basis. JMAP-42pb is a decision record, not a problem. The remaining P2/P3 items have real engineering bases. The forEmailId null validation gap is the one substantive item not yet captured.
Maintainer risk: 8 issues filed (JMAP-86mv, JMAP-22zb, JMAP-2oih, JMAP-4l5d, JMAP-obg9, JMAP-h2wv, JMAP-2k1u, JMAP-2cjh). Summary: (1) case-sensitive Disposition: heuristic vs case-insensitive find_header_value inconsistency; (2) RFC 8098 disposition modifiers (displayed/error) silently drop blobs to notParsable; (3) send_mdns blob hardcodes disposition=displayed regardless of request; (4) serde parse errors discarded in both handlers; (5) parse_mdns hand-built JSON template will silently drop new Mdn fields; (6) TODO comment in committed code on MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS; (7) find_header_value has no RFC 5322 folded-header support; (8) CRLF injection check misses server-set fields (mdn_gateway, original_message_id) on send path. No state leakage between tests. non_exhaustive on types does not block test construction (JSON round-trip workaround is in place and commented). The test coverage only exercises VALID_MDN_BLOB/INVALID_MDN_BLOB as oracles — no round-trip test covers the blob generated by send_mdns.
title: Review round 1: JMAP-7lr MDN implementation
